headline: What to Do if You Suspect Surgical Negligence
articleBody:
It’s a truly frightening experience to undergo surgery hoping for improvement, only to face unexpected complications or injuries that you believe resulted from negligence. The trust you place in medical professionals is profound, and when that trust is broken, the emotional and physical toll can be immense. But please know, you're not alone in this, and there are concrete steps you can take to understand what happened and explore your options.

First things first, prioritize your health. If you're experiencing new or worsening symptoms post-surgery, seek immediate medical attention. Get a clear diagnosis from a different doctor if possible. This isn't about assigning blame yet; it's about ensuring your well-being and understanding the full extent of your current medical condition.

Next, start collecting every piece of information you can. This includes medical records related to your surgery, post-operative care, and any subsequent treatments for complications. Don't be afraid to ask for these documents; they are your right. Keep a detailed personal record too—a journal noting your symptoms, how your life has changed, and any conversations you have with medical staff.
